raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

Follow-up to #44666. This draft targets its branch so the diff shows only this change. I'll retarget it to main once #44666 merges.

On Hopper, Muse Spark runs the pooler (8192 -> 4096) and unpooler (4096 -> 8192) as replicated BF16 GEMMs on every TP rank. At decode sizes these are weight reads: each rank reads 128 MB per layer for the two projections, and all 8 ranks of the H200 TP8 recipe read the same bytes.

`gemm_ag` already column-splits these on SM103, and it runs fine on SM90 (multimem stores need SM90+). Today SM90 only uses it for the unpooler at M <= 8.

## Modifications

- `gemm_ag.projection_max_tokens`: on SM90 with TP4/8, split the 4096-wide pooler up to 512 rows (same as SM103) and the 8192-wide unpooler up to 64 rows. SM103 and other archs are unchanged.
- SM90 has no cluster boundary to defer the unpooler gather into, so the gather runs inline. Past 64 rows the 8192-wide gather costs more than the GEMM saves.
- The pooler call site and the push-workspace reservation accept SM90. The reservation is sized per projection width (4 MB per slot on SM90).
- New multi-GPU test: the gathered output equals each rank's slice GEMM side by side, at M = 1 and at the arch bound, with the reserved push space.

## Accuracy Tests

The split output differs from the replicated GEMM by at most 2 bf16 ulp per element (cuBLAS picks a different kernel for the narrow slice), and is bit-exact for M >= 1024. No accuracy eval with real weights yet.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Component, 8xH200 TP8, CUDA graph, cold weights (rotated past L2), max over ranks per replay, median of 9, us:

| proj | M | replicated | slice GEMM | multicast AG | gemm_ag | ratio |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| pooler | 1 | 21.7 | 6.7 | 7.6 | 16.1 | 0.74 |
| pooler | 8 | 23.0 | 7.5 | 8.9 | 16.1 | 0.70 |
| pooler | 64 | 25.1 | 8.0 | 9.5 | 16.6 | 0.66 |
| pooler | 128 | 27.0 | 9.6 | 11.8 | 20.5 | 0.76 |
| pooler | 256 | 33.4 | 11.1 | 15.3 | 27.1 | 0.81 |
| pooler | 512 | 48.2 | 13.8 | 22.7 | 34.8 | 0.72 |
| unpooler | 16 | 20.0 | 7.3 | 7.8 | 14.8 | 0.74 |
| unpooler | 32 | 20.1 | 7.5 | 9.3 | 16.4 | 0.81 |
| unpooler | 64 | 21.6 | 7.9 | 12.0 | 17.4 | 0.80 |
| unpooler | 128 | 21.9 | 8.4 | 15.2 | 23.6 | 1.08 |
| unpooler | 256 | 27.5 | 10.5 | 23.6 | 33.7 | 1.22 |

End to end, decode step, Muse Spark Open NVFP4 config with dummy weights (all 62 layers), 8xH200 TP8/EP8, `--moe-runner-backend marlin`, decode CUDA graph, `sglang.benchmark.one_batch`, output 32, base and branch interleaved twice in one container, median of 31 steps, ms:

| bs | base | this PR | change |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 12.70 | 11.81 | -7.0% |
| 2 | 13.91 | 12.91 | -7.2% |
| 4 | 16.34 | 15.03 | -8.1% |
| 8 | 18.26 | 17.73 | -2.9% |
| 16 | 22.36 | 21.17 | -5.3% |
| 32 | 24.26 | 23.16 | -4.6% |
| 64 | 32.91 | 31.04 | -5.7% |
| 128 | 42.80 | 42.06 | -1.7% |

bs 1-32 come from a run with input 256 and tighter bounds (pooler 128, unpooler 32), which take the same path at those sizes. bs 64 and 128 come from a run with the final bounds and input 64; its bs 1 gave 12.68 vs 11.89 (-6.2%). Every branch round beat every base round at each bs.

Dummy weights route close to uniformly, which inflates MoE time at larger batches, so the larger-bs percentages are on the low side.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

+def projection_max_tokens(world_size: int, n: int, device: torch.device) -> int:
+    """Largest M that runs as slice GEMM + all-gather instead of a replicated GEMM."""

+"""Muse Spark column-split projection (slice GEMM + multicast all-gather).
+
+The gathered output must equal every rank's slice GEMM placed side by side,
+up to the per-arch row bound, with the push space the model reserves.
+
+Usage::
+
+    python test/registered/kernels/ops/communication/test_muse_spark_gemm_ag.py
+    python test/registered/kernels/ops/communication/test_muse_spark_gemm_ag.py --num-gpu 2
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import atexit
+import os
+
+import pytest
+import torch
+import torch.distributed as dist
+import torch.nn.functional as F
+
+import sglang.srt.distributed.parallel_state as ps
+from sglang.kernels.jit.utils import cache_once
+from sglang.kernels.ops.communication.mp import register_comm_cleanup
+from sglang.kernels.ops.muse_spark import gemm_ag
+from sglang.srt.distributed.device_communicators.custom_all_reduce_v2 import (
+    CustomAllReduceV2,
+)
+from sglang.srt.runtime_context import get_parallel
+from sglang.test.ci.ci_register import register_cuda_ci
+from sglang.test.kernels.utils import multigpu_pytest_main
+
+register_cuda_ci(est_time=60, stage="extra-b", runner_config="8-gpu-h200")
+
+# (K, N) of the pooler and the unpooler.
+_SHAPES = [(8192, 4096), (4096, 8192)]
+
+
+def _device():
+    return torch.device("cuda", int(os.environ["LOCAL_RANK"]))
+
+
+@cache_once
+def _init_comm():
+    local_rank = int(os.environ["LOCAL_RANK"])
+    world_size = int(os.environ["WORLD_SIZE"])
+    torch.cuda.set_device(local_rank)
+    dist.init_process_group(backend="gloo")
+    ps._WORLD = coord = ps.init_world_group(
+        ranks=list(range(world_size)),
+        local_rank=local_rank,
+        backend="nccl",
+    )
+    get_parallel().override_permanently(world_group=coord)
+    atexit.register(dist.destroy_process_group)
+    comm = CustomAllReduceV2(coord.cpu_group, _device())
+    for _, n in _SHAPES:
+        gemm_ag.reserve_projection_workspace(comm, n)
+    register_comm_cleanup(comm)
+    return comm
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("k,n", _SHAPES)
+@torch.inference_mode()
+def test_gemm_ag_matches_slice_gemms(k, n):
+    comm = _init_comm()
+    if comm.disabled or not comm.has_multicast:
+        pytest.skip("needs a multicast-capable NVLink group")
+    max_tokens = gemm_ag.projection_max_tokens(comm.world_size, n, _device())
+    n_local = n // comm.world_size
+    generator = torch.Generator().manual_seed(n)
+    weight = (torch.randn(n, k, generator=generator) * 0.02).to(
+        _device(), torch.bfloat16
+    )
+    for m in sorted({1, max_tokens}):
+        x = torch.randn(m, k, generator=generator).to(_device(), torch.bfloat16)
+        assert gemm_ag.gemm_ag_supported(comm, x, weight)
+        output = gemm_ag.gemm_ag(comm, x, weight)
+        expected = torch.cat(
+            [
+                F.linear(x, weight[rank * n_local : (rank + 1) * n_local])
+                for rank in range(comm.world_size)
+            ],
+            dim=1,
+        )
+        torch.cuda.synchronize()
+        assert torch.equal(output, expected), f"{m=}"
+    past_bound = torch.empty(max_tokens + 1, k, device=_device(), dtype=torch.bfloat16)
+    assert not gemm_ag.gemm_ag_supported(comm, past_bound, weight)
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    multigpu_pytest_main(__name__, __file__, num_gpus=(8,))
